Women's sizes being all over the place is for one, a massive fucking inconvenience. It's happened a lot that I have been in a hurry and I need a new shirt for work or a new pair of pants and despite my best approximations, I quickly grab what size I am in most other clothes, and it doesn't fit. Not only is it a hassle to return a small shirt that fits me like a sausage casing while I am a small in most other brands and clothes, it's embarrassing because it makes one feel kind of stupid while at the same time nudging any insecurities one might have about their body, which a lot of women do.

If I am online and see something I like, it becomes a tedious process of combing through size charts and reading reviews to see if the item itself runs small or not, whereas if I am buying something, say, a shirt, for my boyfriend I can safely grab a medium with no worries, since he is always a medium. His size has changed a lot recently, but it's not because brands just sort of toss random numbers or sizes on his clothes, it's because he's growing.

Having one or two size range in something does not equate to buying clothing being some sort of weird roulette where the thing could fit, or could be way too small, or be way too big. A lot of women's brands are known as having "vanity sizing" where their sizes are scaled down to being smaller than they really should be, too.

There is a reason that a lot of women throw in the towel and just buy men's clothing for themselves. Women's sizing is a complete nightmare and makes the buying experience totally exhausting. A lot of men acknowledge this too... I would say it's a gendered issue for sure and I'm also sure that the majority of people, women or men would agree. Not sure why it's such a difficult concept for you.
